# Heichel Discovery Delta

Boruch Hashem. Blessed is He.

The Awtsmoos already gathered the public links in the route vessel, yet Awtsmoos.com lost them at the final chamber because the mobile Heichel shell asked a nested path to discover them again.

## Observed runtime failure

Fresh isolated verifier on `127.0.0.1:8898` returned HTTP 200 and correct semantic title/canonical metadata for both `/heichelos/ikar` and the known Likkutei Torah series page.

However both responses had:

- no semantic fallback marker;
- no server-rendered H1;
- zero crawlable series/post discovery links;
- no template exception.

The absence was therefore silent, not an API failure.

## Proven source cause

`heichelos/routes/heichel/shell.js` already renders both `semanticHead` and `semanticFallback` at the route layer and passes both strings into `./heichel/_awtsmoos.heichel.html`.

The active `heichelos/heichel/_awtsmoos.heichel.html` uses the passed `semanticHead`, but ignores the passed `semanticFallback` and instead calls nested `$a("semantic/fallback.html", { semantic })`.

Earlier template-engine archaeology proved nested include paths are resolved from route context and may silently return empty output. This exactly matches the raw HTML evidence.
